Hi Elena — thanks for the note and context. Short answer: yes, we can do an add-on now and co-term it to your Jan 1 renewal. I put together three pragmatic paths below (attached workbook has the line-item math):

Option A — Fast top-up (no annual commitment change):
- Add 25% capacity immediately at list rate pro-rated for remainder of the year.
- No change to renewal; standard renewal pricing applies.
- Use when you want the simplest procurement path.

Option B — Top-up + Renewal Commitment (preferred economics):
- Add 25% now and commit to a 12-month uplift at renewal (effective Jan 1) with a blended discount of 10% across new total ARR; immediate add-on billed pro-rata at 50% discount as a courtesy.
- Requires an internal ARR commitment to be documented in the SOW.

Option C — Bridge + Annualize (min friction, improved unit price):
- Bridge top-up now as a convertible credit; credits applied against Jan invoice and annualized into new committed units at 12% discount on incremental units only.
- Best if procurement wants to avoid midterm amendment complexity but still capture savings.

I've looped in Ben (pricing lead) to confirm margin impact and whether Legal will need an amendment now or at renewal. Attached: Nebula_Topup_Options_v3.xlsx (detailed math) and a draft SOW scaffold.

Would you prefer we surface a single recommend path + redline-ready amendment, or all three options in a single package for procurement?
